record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: What types of dynamics should models of social organizations include when calculating resilience? The question should include concurrent changes in network topology and processes on networks, entry and exit of agents, restructuring, temporal paths, and internal or external shocks whose timing may overlap normal organizational dynamics.

evidence.quote: Questions • What types of dynamics do we consider for social organizations?

Instead, the diﬀerent processes discussed below should be seen as concurrent. This leads to a number of issues, such as overlapping or sliding time windows, choice of the appropriate time scale for aggregation, etc.
Because of the volatile dynamics, we cannot clearly separate shocks from the ‘normal’ dynamics, which both occur on the same time scale.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is framed as an open conceptual problem in the modeling of social resilience: existing literature on temporal networks, adaptive networks, and resilience metrics addresses individual aspects (topology change, processes on networks, temporal paths, shock response) but no unified framework integrating all listed ingredients with a provably well-defined resilience measure appears to be established. No source verifying a complete solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Presents resilience modeling for social organizations as a set of open problems involving concurrent dynamics, entry/exit, and shocks overlapping normal dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open modeling challenge.
